what_it_measured.text: Aims: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) management with basal insulin can lead to hypoglycaemia and weight gain.

In this context, we aimed to investigate the efficacy and safety of OW s.c. semaglutide 2.0 mg as an add-on to dosereduced IGlar U100 (Sema+IGlar reduced) versus dosetitrated IGlar U100 without semaglutide (IGlar titrated) in people with T2D and overweight, suggesting that it would be a more efficacious and safer alternative for achieving glycaemic control with a lower risk of weight gain and hypoglycaemia.

dose.text: The SUSTAIN 5 and SUSTAIN FORTE studies highlight the limitations of basal insulin–centred intensification strategies and a dosedependent effect, with the 2.0 mg semaglutide dose providing superior efficacy versus 1.0 mg.

SUSTAIN 5 provided valuable insight into the effects of semaglutide as an add-on to basal insulin on glycaemic control, whereby it was found that OW s.c. semaglutide 0.5 and 1.0 mg doses were both superior to placebo in reducing HbA1c and BW [12].

route.text: In this context, we aimed to investigate the efficacy and safety of OW s.c. semaglutide 2.0 mg as an add-on to dosereduced IGlar U100 (Sema+IGlar reduced) versus dosetitrated IGlar U100 without semaglutide (IGlar titrated) in people with T2D and overweight, suggesting that it would be a more efficacious and safer alternative for achieving glycaemic control with a lower risk of weight gain and hypoglycaemia.

Moreover, the SUSTAIN FORTE trial investigated the intensification of OW s.c. semaglutide treatment (2.0 vs. 1.0 mg) in people with T2D, wherein OW s.c. semaglutide 2.0 mg was superior to 1.0 mg in reducing HbA 1c and BW [14].

SUSTAIN 5 provided valuable insight into the effects of semaglutide as an add-on to basal insulin on glycaemic control, whereby it was found that OW s.c. semaglutide 0.5 and 1.0 mg doses were both superior to placebo in reducing HbA1c and BW [12].

endpoint.text: Secondary endpoints assessed superiority of Sema+IGlarreduced versus IGlartitrated in reducing HbA1c, BW, daily insulin dose, and improving Diabetes Treatment Satisfaction Questionnaire change version (DTSQc) scores.
The primary endpoint was change in HbA1c using a non-inferiority approach.

For the semaglutide treatment arm, participants received SMBG- guided titration during the first 12weeks (which was consistent with the dose- titrated comparator) while simultaneously undergoing IGlar de- escalation, followed by titration- only from week 12 to end of trial (EoT). 2.4 | Outcomes The primary endpoint was change in HbA1c (%-points) from baseline to week 40, tested for non- inferiority of Sema+IGlarreduced compared to IGlartitrated, where a predetermined non- inferiority margin of 0.3%- points for HbA1c treatment difference was judged as being a clinically acceptable loss of efficacy compared to IGlartitrated in the context of expected benefits.

reported_results.text: Conclusions: Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 2.0 mg as add-on to dose-reduced IGlar achieved superior reductions in HbA1c, BW, and daily insulin dose in people with T2D and overweight, while reducing their risk for severe hypoglycaemia compared to dose-titrated IGlar alone.
Severe hypoglycaemia was reduced (rate ratio: 0.45; CI95: 0.23, 0.87; p = 0.02), while gastrointestinal events were higher for Sema+IGlarreduced (310 vs. 32 events).

Sema+IGlarreduced achieved both non-inferiority and superiority versus IGlartitrated in HbA1c reduction (estimated treatment difference [ETD]: −0.74%; 95% confidence interval [CI95]: −0.90, −0.59) and superiority in BW change (ETD: −8.5 kg; CI95: −9.5, −7.4), relative daily insulin dose change (ETD: −121.9%; CI95: −143.1, −100.6), and DTSQc scores (ETD: 2.6; CI95: 1.6, 3.5) (p < 0.0001 for all endpoints).

SUSTAIN OPTIMIZE compared once-weekly semaglutide 2.0 mg as add-on to dose-reduced insulin glargine (Sema+IGlarreduced) versus dose-titrated IGlar (IGlartitrated) on glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), body weight (BW), daily insulin dose, and participant satisfaction.
The ETD for Sema+IGlar reduced versus IGlar titrated was −0.74% (95% CI: −0.90 to −0.59; p < 0.0001 for noninferiority) (Figure 1A).
